children: The yen's rebound seems to be built on shaky ground, says Bank J. Safra Sarasin's Claudio Wewel. The Japanese currency has weakened to 158 against the dollar, reviving intervention chatter as markets weigh the prospects of more global rate hikes. Wewel reckons that the yen will likely remain around 160 near term as the BOJ's more hawkish shift is probably not enough for a sustained recovery. The BOJ signaling faster hikes is chipping away at perceptions of the central bank as slow-moving--a long-standing drag on the yen. But recent market reactions show that it may still be too slow relative to other G-10 central banks, Wewel says. In spite of several bullish catalysts, he cautions that headwinds persist, including strong U.S. macro data, high energy prices and concerns over the sustainability of Japanese debt. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
